questions.text: मानव में गर्भ उत्क्षेपन प्रतिवर्त (फीटल इजेक्शन रेफलेक्स) _______ हॉर्मोन के _______ द्वारा स्रवण (विमोचन) को उद्दीपित करता है।
questions.text_english: The foetal ejection reflex in human triggers the release of _______ hormone from _______.
questions.instruction_line: सही विकल्प का चयन कर रिक्त स्थानों की पूर्ति कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Fill in the blanks by choosing right option.
questions.solution: The foetal ejection reflex induces mild uterine contractions, which in turn trigger the massive release of the oxytocin hormone directly from the maternal pituitary gland. This oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle to cause stronger contractions leading to parturition.
questions.solution_hindi: गर्भ उत्क्षेपन प्रतिवर्त गर्भाशय के संकुचन को प्रेरित करता है, जो मातृ पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन हॉर्मोन के अत्यधिक स्राव को उद्दीपित करता है।

questions.text:
कॉलम I में दी गई अंतः गर्भाशयी युक्तियों (आईयूडी) का कॉलम II में दिए गए उपयुक्त उदाहरण के साथ मिलान कीजिए।
कॉलम I
a. औषधि-रहित
b. ताँबा मोचक
c. हॉर्मोन मोचक

कॉलम II
i. लिप्पेस लूप
ii. एलएनजी-20
iii. मल्टीलोड 375
questions.text_english:
Match the IUDs in Column I with suitable example in Column II.
Column I
a. Non-medicated
b. Copper releasing
c. Hormone releasing

Column II
i. Lippes loop
ii. LNG-20
iii. Multiload 375
questions.solution: Lippes loop is a classic example of a non-medicated IUD. Multiload 375 is a well-known copper-releasing IUD. LNG-20 is a specialized hormone-releasing IUD. Thus, matching 'a' with 'i', 'b' with 'iii', and 'c' with 'ii' is the correct combination.
questions.solution_hindi: लिप्पेस लूप (Lippes loop) एक औषधि-रहित IUD है। मल्टीलोड 375 एक ताँबा मोचक IUD है। एलएनजी-20 (LNG-20) एक हॉर्मोन मोचक IUD है। अतः a का i से, b का iii से और c का ii से मिलान सही है।

questions.text: पाइसम सेटाइवम में, पुष्प का रंग बैंगनी (V) अथवा श्वेत (v) हो सकता है। 'VV' पौधे तथा 'vv' पौधे के मध्य संकरण कराने के फलस्वरूप बैंगनी रंग के पुष्पों वाली संतति का अपेक्षित आनुपातिक भाग क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english: In Pisum sativum, the flower colour may be violet (V) or white (v). What proportion of the offspring in a cross of VV x vv would be expected to be violet?
questions.solution: In a Mendelian monohybrid cross between a homozygous dominant parent (VV) and a homozygous recessive parent (vv), all offspring in the F1 generation will possess the heterozygous genotype (Vv). Because the violet trait is dominant over white, 100% of the resulting offspring will exhibit the violet flower phenotype.
questions.solution_hindi: समयुग्मजी प्रभावी 'VV' और समयुग्मजी अप्रभावी 'vv' के बीच संकरण कराने पर F1 पीढ़ी की सभी संततियाँ विषमयुग्मजी 'Vv' होंगी। चूँकि बैंगनी रंग प्रभावी है, अतः 100% संततियों में बैंगनी रंग के पुष्प होंगे।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित को विकास के सही क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प चुनिए : (i) समुद्री खरपतवार (ii) अकशेरुकी (iii) जबड़े रहित मछली
questions.text_english: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of their evolution and select the correct option: (i) Seaweed (ii) Invertebrates (iii) Jawless fish
questions.solution: According to the geological time scale and evolutionary history, invertebrates were formed and became active around 500 million years ago. Jawless fish evolved later, around 350 million years ago. Seaweeds and a few terrestrial plants existed around 320 million years ago. Therefore, the correct evolutionary sequence is (ii) Invertebrates, (iii) Jawless fish, and (i) Seaweed.
questions.solution_hindi: विकास के सही क्रम के अनुसार, अकशेरुकी (लगभग 500 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व) सबसे पहले आए, उसके बाद जबड़े रहित मछली (लगभग 350 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व) और अंत में समुद्री खरपतवार (लगभग 320 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व)। सही क्रम (ii), (iii), (i) है।

questions.text: सामान्य दृश्यप्ररूप (फीनोटाइप) वाली संवाहक स्त्री से यदि आनुवंशिक विकार कुछ नर संतति में स्थानांतरित (वंशागत) होती है, तो रोग है :
questions.text_english: If a genetic disease is transferred from a phenotypically normal but carrier female to only some of the male progeny, the disease is :
questions.solution: The pattern where a phenotypically normal mother acts as a carrier and transmits the disease exclusively to her sons is the hallmark of a sex-linked recessive disorder (such as haemophilia or colour blindness). Because males possess only one X chromosome, inheriting the single defective allele from the carrier mother is sufficient to cause the disease.
questions.solution_hindi: वह वंशागति प्रतिरूप जिसमें एक सामान्य दिखने वाली लेकिन संवाहक (carrier) माँ बीमारी को विशेष रूप से अपने पुत्रों (नर संतति) में स्थानांतरित करती है, लिंग-सहलग्न अप्रभावी (sex-linked recessive) विकार की पहचान है (जैसे हीमोफीलिया या वर्णांधता)। चूँकि पुरुषों में केवल एक X गुणसूत्र होता है, माँ से एक भी दोषपूर्ण एलील प्राप्त करना बीमारी पैदा करने के लिए पर्याप्त है।

questions.text: एक डीएनए अणु 160 क्षार युग्म लंबा है। इसमें ग्वानीन 30% है। इस डीएनए अणु में ऐडेनीन क्षार की संख्या कितनी है ?
questions.text_english: A DNA molecule is 160 base pairs long. It has 30% Guanine. How many Adenine bases are present in this DNA molecule ?
questions.solution: A DNA molecule that is 160 base pairs long contains a total of 320 nitrogenous bases. According to Chargaff's rule, if Guanine (G) is 30%, then Cytosine (C) is also 30%, making GC content 60%. The remaining 40% represents Adenine (A) and Thymine (T) combined. Therefore, Adenine makes up 20% of the total bases. 20% of 320 bases equals 64 Adenine bases.
questions.solution_hindi: 160 क्षार युग्म लंबे डीएनए अणु में कुल 320 क्षार होंगे। चारगाफ के नियम के अनुसार, यदि ग्वानीन (G) 30% है, तो साइटोसिन (C) भी 30% होगा। शेष 40% एडेनिन (A) और थाइमिन (T) होंगे। इस प्रकार, एडेनिन 20% होगा। 320 क्षारों का 20% 64 होता है।

questions.text: एक चिकित्सक ने एक रोगी में नासीय संकुलता (नेजल कंजेशन), सिरदर्द, कंठदाह, स्वर रूक्षता तथा खाँसी के लक्षणों के आधार पर निष्कर्ष निकाला कि रोगी का संक्रमण एक रोगकारक (रोगजनक) द्वारा हुआ है। वह रोगजनक है :
questions.text_english: A doctor identifies symptoms of nasal congestion, headache, sore throat, hoarseness and cough in a patient. The conclusion is that the patient is infected by a pathogen:
questions.solution: The symptoms described—nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, and headache—are characteristic of the common cold. The common cold is primarily caused by a group of viruses known as rhinoviruses.
questions.solution_hindi: बताए गए लक्षण—नासीय संकुलता (नाक बंद होना), सिरदर्द, कंठदाह (गले में खराश), स्वर रूक्षता और खाँसी—सामान्य जुकाम (common cold) की विशेषता हैं। सामान्य जुकाम मुख्य रूप से राइनोवायरस (Rhinoviruses) नामक विषाणुओं के समूह के कारण होता है।

questions.text: शलभ (मॉथ), बिस्टन बिटूलेरिया में प्रेक्षित औद्योगिक मेलेनिनीकरण किस प्रकार का वरण है ?
questions.text_english: Which type of selection is industrial melanism observed in moth, Biston betularia?
questions.solution: Industrial melanism in the peppered moth (Biston betularia) is a classic example of directional selection. During the industrial revolution, as pollution darkened tree trunks, the environment selectively favored the darker (melanic) moths over the lighter ones, causing a steady, directional shift in the population's phenotype over time.
questions.solution_hindi: पेपर्ड मॉथ (बिस्टन बिटूलेरिया) में औद्योगिक मेलेनिनीकरण दिशिक वरण (Directional selection) का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। औद्योगिक क्रांति के दौरान, प्रदूषण के कारण पेड़ों के तने काले हो गए, जिससे पर्यावरण ने हल्के रंग के पतंगों की तुलना में गहरे (मेलेनिक) रंग के पतंगों को संरक्षण प्रदान किया, जिससे समय के साथ आबादी के दृश्यप्ररूप (फेनोटाइप) में एक दिशा में बदलाव आया।

questions.text: मानव इंसुलिन का सी-पेप्टाइड :
questions.text_english: C-peptide of human insulin is :

options.A: परिपक्व इंसुलिन के अणु का एक भाग है।
options.B: डाइसल्फाइड बंध बनाकर संयोजित करने के लिए उत्तरदायी है।
options.C: प्राक् इंसुलिन के इंसुलिन में परिपक्व होने की अवधि में हटा (विलग) दिया जाता है।
options.D: इसकी जैवीय सक्रियता के लिए उत्तरदायी है।

options_english.A: a part of mature insulin molecule.
options_english.B: responsible for formation of disulphide bridges.
options_english.C: removed during maturation of pro-insulin to insulin.

questions.solution: In mammals, including humans, insulin is initially synthesized as a precursor called pro-insulin, which contains an extra stretch of amino acids called the C-peptide. This C-peptide is strictly removed during the maturation process to form the final, active insulin molecule. Thus, it is not present in mature insulin.
questions.solution_hindi: मनुष्यों सहित स्तनधारियों में, इंसुलिन शुरू में प्राक् इंसुलिन (pro-insulin) के रूप में संश्लेषित होता है, जिसमें सी-पेप्टाइड (C-peptide) नामक अमीनो एसिड का एक अतिरिक्त खंड होता है। अंतिम, सक्रिय इंसुलिन अणु बनाने के लिए परिपक्वता प्रक्रिया के दौरान इस सी-पेप्टाइड को हटा (विलग कर) दिया जाता है।

questions.text: एक डीएनए अणु पर एक प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ Pst I तथा विदलन स्थलों को निम्न रूप से दर्शाया गया है। 5' C-T-G-C-A+G 3' / 3' G+A-C-G-T-C 5'. उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जो परिणामी खंडों का सही निरूपण करता है।
questions.text_english: Given below is the restriction site of a restriction endonuclease Pst I and the cleavage sites on a DNA molecule. 5' C-T-G-C-A+G 3' / 3' G+A-C-G-T-C 5'. Choose the option that gives the correct resultant fragments.
questions.solution: The restriction enzyme Pst I identifies the sequence 5'-CTGCAG-3' and produces a staggered cut specifically between the Adenine (A) and Guanine (G) bases. Following the cleavage marks provided, the cut separates the 5' CTGCA segment from the 3' G on the top strand, and the 3' G segment from the 5' ACGTC on the bottom strand. This leads exactly to the fragments shown in option D.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ Pst I डीएनए अनुक्रम में एडेनिन (A) और ग्वानीन (G) के बीच एक असमान कट उत्पन्न करता है। दिए गए कट निशानों के आधार पर, यह शीर्ष रज्जुक पर 5' CTGCA और 3' G को अलग करता है, और निचले रज्जुक पर 3' G और 5' ACGTC को अलग करता है। यह परिणामी खंड विकल्प D में स्पष्ट रूप से दिखाई दे रहे हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी मछली के कारण पूर्वी अफ्रीका की विक्टोरिया झील में पारिस्थितिक रूप से बेजोड़ सिचलिड मछलियों की 200 से अधिक जातियाँ विलुप्त हो गईं ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following fish led to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in Lake Victoria of East Africa?
questions.solution: The catastrophic extinction of more than 200 endemic species of cichlid fish in Lake Victoria was directly triggered by the deliberate human introduction of a large, highly aggressive alien predator species known as the Nile Perch.
questions.solution_hindi: पूर्वी अफ्रीका की विक्टोरिया झील में एक बड़ी और आक्रामक विदेशी शिकारी मछली, नाइल पर्च (Nile Perch) के प्रवेश के कारण पारिस्थितिक रूप से बेजोड़ सिचलिड मछलियों की 200 से अधिक प्रजातियाँ विलुप्त हो गईं।

questions.text: चारण पशुओं (मवेशी) अथवा बकरियों को कैलोट्रॉपिस नामक खरपतवार को खाते (चरते) हुए कभी भी नहीं देखा गया है। कारण के लिए समुचित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Cattle or goats are never seen browsing on the weed, Calotropis. Select the correct option for the reason.

options.A: पौधा अत्यंत विषैले टेनिन उत्पन्न करता है।
options.B: पौधा कुनैन उत्पन्न करता है जो अत्यंत कड़वा होता है।
options.C: पौधा हृदय ग्लाइकोसाइड नामक विषैला रसायन उत्पन्न करता है।

options_english.A: The plant produces highly poisonous tannins.
options_english.B: The plant produces quinine, which is bitter in taste.
options_english.C: The plant produces the poisonous chemical, cardiac glycoside.

questions.solution: The weed Calotropis is avoided by all grazing animals like cattle and goats because it produces a highly toxic chemical compound known as cardiac glycoside. This profound chemical defense mechanism effectively deters herbivores.
questions.solution_hindi: कैलोट्रॉपिस (आक) खरपतवार को मवेशी या बकरियां कभी नहीं खाते हैं क्योंकि यह पौधा 'हृदय ग्लाइकोसाइड' (cardiac glycoside) नामक एक अत्यधिक विषैला रसायन उत्पन्न करता है, जो शाकाहारियों के लिए घातक हो सकता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : पुनरावृत्ति अनुक्रम मानव जीनोम का बहुत बड़ा भाग बनाते हैं।
कारण (R) : जीनोम में पुनरावृत्ति अनुक्रम प्रत्यक्ष रूप से कोडिंग (कूटलेखन) नहीं करते।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Repetitive sequences make up a very large portion of human genome.
Reason (R): Repetitive sequences do not have direct coding functions in the genome.
questions.instruction_line:
प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं- जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन प्रश्नों के सही उत्तर नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चुनकर दीजिए।
(A) अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(B) अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
(C) अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
(D) अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english:
For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.
(A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

questions.solution: Repetitive DNA sequences indeed constitute a vastly significant portion of the human genome. questions.text_english: State the role of thymus as a lymphoid organ. Name the cells that are released from it and mention their functions.

key_points: State role: Thymus acts as a primary lymphoid organ providing the necessary micro-environment for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.

questions.solution: The thymus is classified fundamentally as a primary lymphoid organ. Its critical biological role is to provide a highly specialized micro-environment that explicitly facilitates the differentiation and complete maturation of T-lymphocytes. The fully mature cells actively released from the thymus are specifically known as T-lymphocytes (or T-cells). The primary immunological function of these released T-cells is to aggressively orchestrate and execute Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI), which effectively destroys virus-infected cells and rejects foreign grafts; they also provide essential assistance to B-cells to synthesize antibodies.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Explain the mutually rewarding relationship between Yucca plant and species of moth.

key_points: Explain Mutualism: Both species heavily depend on each other to complete their life cycles.
Reward to Moth: The moth uses the plant's ovarian locule as a completely safe biological space to lay its eggs.

sub_questions.solution: The Yucca plant and a highly specific species of moth exhibit a classic example of obligate mutualism, wherein neither organism can successfully complete its life cycle without the other. The rewarding relationship operates flawlessly: the moth gains a secure, sheltered environment by depositing its eggs deeply within the locule of the Yucca's ovary. Concurrently, the Yucca plant is massively rewarded because, during the deliberate process of egg-laying, the moth actively transfers pollen, ensuring the essential pollination of the flower. Later, as the plant's seeds begin developing, the moth larvae safely hatch and feed on a few seeds.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Pollination success will be reduced unless the orchid flower co-evolves with the pollinator. Explain.

key_points: Explain co-evolution: The specialized floral structure is closely linked to the specific morphology of the pollinator.
Give example: The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs 'sexual deceit' where its petal precisely mimics a female bee.

Explain impact of no co-evolution: If the female bee slightly changes her morphological pattern through evolution and the orchid fails to simultaneously co-evolve to match it, the male bee will no longer be deceived, completely halting pollination.

sub_questions.solution: In highly specialized plant-pollinator relationships, extreme co-evolution is absolutely critical for reproductive success. A fascinating example is the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys, which brilliantly employs 'sexual deceit' to guarantee pollination. One of its petals has evolved to bear an uncanny physical and chemical resemblance to a specific female bee. Male bees, heavily attracted to this mimic, 'pseudocopulate' with the flower and inadvertently transfer pollen. However, if the actual female bee undergoes any evolutionary morphological changes, the pollination success of the orchid will be catastrophically reduced to zero, unless the orchid flower simultaneously co-evolves to perfectly match the new morphological pattern of the female bee.

OR

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Differentiate between grazing food chain and detritus food chain.

key_points: Difference 1: Grazing food chain strictly begins with living green plants (producers) utilizing solar energy. Detritus food chain begins completely with dead organic matter (detritus).
Difference 2: The primary consumers in a grazing food chain are herbivores. The primary consumers in a detritus food chain are saprotrophs/decomposers like bacteria and fungi.

sub_questions.solution: The fundamental difference between the Grazing Food Chain (GFC) and the Detritus Food Chain (DFC) lies in their absolute starting points. The GFC always begins directly with living green plants (producers) that capture and utilize primary solar energy, passing it onward to herbivores. In stark contrast, the DFC originates completely with dead organic matter (detritus), such as fallen leaves or dead animals, and the energy is subsequently processed by specialized saprotrophs and decomposers, like fungi and bacteria.

sub_questions.text: (ख) यद्यपि पारिस्थितिक पिरैमिड (सूची स्तंभ) व्यापक रूप से स्वीकार्य हैं, फिर भी उनकी कुछ सीमाएँ हैं। कोई दो सीमाएँ लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Ecological pyramids are widely accepted but they still have some limitations. Write any two limitations.

key_points: Limitation 1: They entirely assume a simplistic, linear food chain that almost never physically exists in nature, completely failing to accommodate complex food webs.
Limitation 2: They do not assign any specific level or place to highly crucial saprophytes/decomposers despite their immense role in energy recycling.
Limitation 3: They fail to properly account for versatile species that may simultaneously belong to two or more distinct trophic levels.

sub_questions.solution: Despite their widespread educational use, ecological pyramids harbor significant biological limitations. First, they rigidly assume the existence of a simplistic, linear food chain, completely failing to accurately accommodate the overlapping complexity of real-world food webs. Second, they entirely fail to assign any specific trophic level or structural place to saprophytes and decomposers, even though these organisms play a tremendously vital and continuous role in ecosystem energy recycling. Furthermore, they struggle to accurately account for highly versatile species, like omnivores, which simultaneously operate across multiple distinct trophic levels.

questions.solution: This question allows the student to either contrast differing types of ecological food chains or explain the inherent structural limitations of ecological pyramids.

questions.text_english: How do 'implants' act as an effective method of contraception in human females? Mention one advantage of implants over contraceptive pills.

key_points: Explain mechanism: Implants continuously release progestogens (or combined with estrogen) into the blood, inhibiting ovulation and altering cervical mucus to prevent sperm entry.
State advantage: Implants are effective for much longer periods (long acting) and do not require the daily administration discipline that pills demand.

questions.solution: Subcutaneous implants act as highly effective contraceptives because they contain progestogens (or a combination of progestogen and estrogen) which are slowly and steadily released into the bloodstream over time. This continuous hormonal release effectively inhibits ovulation and thickens cervical mucus, making it hostile to sperm entry. A major advantage of implants over traditional daily oral contraceptive pills is their long-term efficacy; once inserted under the skin, they provide uninterrupted protection for several years without relying on the user's daily memory and compliance.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Explain any two methods of vectorless gene transfer.

key_points: Method 1: Microinjection - Recombinant DNA is physically forced and directly injected into the naked nucleus of an animal cell using microscopic needles.
Method 2: Biolistics (Gene gun) - Plant cells are violently bombarded with high-velocity, microscopic microparticles of gold or tungsten heavily coated with the desired DNA.

sub_questions.solution: Vectorless gene transfer completely bypasses the need for biological plasmids or viruses. Two prominent methods are widely used. The first is Microinjection, a highly delicate physical process primarily utilized for animal cells, where the recombinant DNA solution is forcibly and directly injected straight into the nucleus of the target cell using specialized microscopic needles. The second is the Biolistics or Gene gun method, which is exceptionally suitable for tough plant cells; here, target cells are violently bombarded with high-velocity, microscopic microparticles (typically gold or tungsten) that are heavily coated with the desired foreign DNA.

sub_questions.solution: The most commonly utilized bioreactor in the biotechnology industry is the Stirred-tank bioreactor. questions.text: ध्रुवणता दर्शाते हुए 'प्रतिकृति द्विशाख' का नामांकित आरेख बनाइए । डीएनए प्रतिकृतियन इस प्रकार के 'द्विशाख (चिमटे)' जैसा क्यों होता है ?
questions.text_english: Draw a labelled diagram of a 'replicating fork' showing the polarity. Why does DNA replication occur within such 'fork'?

key_points: Draw a Y-shaped replicating fork accurately indicating template polarities (3'->5' and 5'->3')
Draw and label the continuous (leading) strand being synthesized on the 3'->5' template
Draw and label the discontinuous (lagging) strand with Okazaki fragments on the 5'->3' template
Explain why: The two strands of the massive DNA double helix cannot be separated entirely at once due to the excessively high energy requirement.
Conclude that replication must therefore occur in these small, localized openings of the DNA helix, generating a fork-like structure.

questions.solution: A labelled diagram of the replicating fork must distinctly exhibit a Y-shaped unwound DNA segment. The template strand with 3' to 5' polarity should show a continuous, newly synthesized leading strand moving smoothly towards the fork. Conversely, the template strand with 5' to 3' polarity should display a discontinuous lagging strand forming discrete Okazaki fragments. The process of DNA replication intrinsically forms this distinct 'fork' structure because the two intertwined strands of the massive DNA double helix are exceptionally long. Consequently, they simply cannot be unzipped or separated entirely along their entire length at once, as doing so would demand an impossibly high energy expenditure. Therefore, the helix is unzipped only in small, localized sections, creating the characteristic small opening referred to biologically as the replicating fork.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिकृति द्विशाख (Replicating fork) का नामांकित आरेख Y-आकार का होना चाहिए, जिसमें टेम्प्लेट की ध्रुवता (3'->5' और 5'->3') स्पष्ट हो। 3'->5' टेम्प्लेट पर सतत (अग्रगामी) रज्जुक और 5'->3' टेम्प्लेट पर असतत (पश्चगामी) रज्जुक (ओकाजाकी खंडों के साथ) को दर्शाया जाना चाहिए। डीएनए प्रतिकृतियन द्विशाख में इसलिए होता है क्योंकि डीएनए का डबल हेलिक्स अणु बहुत लंबा होता है। अत्यधिक ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता के कारण इसके दोनों रज्जुकों को एक ही बार में पूरी लंबाई तक अलग नहीं किया जा सकता है। इसलिए, प्रतिकृति डीएनए हेलिक्स के छोटे-छोटे खुले हुए हिस्सों में होती है, जिसे प्रतिकृति द्विशाख कहा जाता है।

questions.text: ऐसी किन्हीं तीन बहि:प्रजनन युक्तियों की सूची बनाइए जो पर-परागण हेतु पुष्पी पादपों द्वारा विकसित की गई हैं तथा व्याख्या कीजिए कि वे पर-परागण को किस प्रकार प्रोत्साहित करती हैं।
questions.text_english: List any three outbreeding devices that flowering plants have developed for cross-pollination and explain how they help to encourage cross-pollination.

key_points: Device 1: Dichogamy (Non-synchronization) - Pollen release and stigma receptivity are deliberately not synchronized, meaning when pollen is released, the stigma is unready, making autogamy impossible.

Device 2: Herkogamy (Spatial separation) - The anther and stigma are placed at entirely different physical positions within the flower, preventing pollen from physically reaching the stigma of the same flower.

Device 3: Self-incompatibility - A strict genetic mechanism that biochemically prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules by actively inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

questions.solution:
To actively prevent continuous inbreeding depression, flowering plants have evolved several ingenious outbreeding devices. 
First is Dichogamy, a precise timing mechanism where pollen release and stigma receptivity are deliberately non-synchronized. The anthers may mature long before the stigma is ready, completely preventing self-pollination (autogamy) and forcing reliance on foreign pollen. 
Second is Herkogamy, which involves a profound spatial separation. The anthers and the stigma are physically placed at entirely different spatial positions within the flower, ensuring that pollen cannot physically fall onto or reach the stigma of the same flower, necessitating a pollinator's intervention. 
Third is Self-incompatibility, an advanced biochemical and genetic mechanism. It actively prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or another flower on the same plant) from fertilizing the ovules by chemically inhibiting pollen germination or violently arresting pollen tube growth deep within the pistil, guaranteeing that only cross-pollinated pollen succeeds.
questions.solution_hindi:
अंतःप्रजनन अवनमन (inbreeding depression) को रोकने के लिए पुष्पी पादपों ने कई बहि: प्रजनन युक्तियाँ विकसित की हैं: 
1) भिन्नकालपक्वता (Dichogamy): इसमें परागकणों के मुक्त होने और वर्तिकाग्र (stigma) के ग्राह्य होने का समय अलग-अलग होता है। यह स्व-परागण (autogamy) को पूरी तरह रोकता है।
2) पृथक्पक्वता (Herkogamy): इसमें परागकोष और वर्तिकाग्र फूल में अलग-अलग भौतिक स्थानों पर स्थित होते हैं, जिससे एक ही फूल का पराग अपने ही वर्तिकाग्र तक भौतिक रूप से नहीं पहुँच सकता।
3) स्व-अयोग्यता (Self-incompatibility): यह एक विशिष्ट आनुवंशिक और जैव रासायनिक तंत्र है जो स्व-परागकणों को अंडाशय में निषेचन करने से रोकता है। यह वर्तिकाग्र पर स्व-परागकणों के अंकुरण या पराग नलिका के विकास को बाधित करता है, जिससे केवल पर-परागण ही सफल हो पाता है।

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Bacillus thuringiensis

key_points: Explain that it produces toxic protein crystals.
State that these toxins are ingested by susceptible insect larvae.
Detail that in the alkaline gut of the insect, the toxin becomes active, binds to midgut cells, creates pores, and causes cell lysis, ultimately killing the insect.

sub_questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis acts as a highly potent biocontrol agent because it naturally produces specific toxic protein crystals during its growth phase. These biological toxins are typically available as dried spores. When vulnerable insect larvae ingest these spores while feeding on sprayed crops, the highly alkaline pH of the insect's gut instantly solubilizes and activates the dormant toxin. The activated toxin tightly binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, physically creating large pores that cause severe cell swelling and lysis, inevitably leading to the rapid death of the pest.

Explain that they are excellent, narrow-spectrum biological insecticides that exclusively target specific insects and arthropods.

sub_questions.solution: Nucleopolyhedrovirus is a specialized genus of baculoviruses that serve as extraordinarily effective biocontrol agents. They function as highly specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal applications, meaning they aggressively attack and destroy only specifically targeted pest insects and arthropods. Crucially, they have been proven to have absolutely no detrimental or negative impacts on surrounding non-target organisms, including plants, mammals, birds, fish, or beneficial insects, making them heavily favored in Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programs.

questions.text_english: Transgenic animals are produced by man. Explain any three ways in which such animals can be beneficial to humans.

key_points: Way 1: Study of Normal Physiology and Development - They are specifically designed to study how genes are regulated and how they deeply affect normal bodily functions.

Way 2: Study of Disease - They serve as invaluable biological models for complex human diseases (like cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis) facilitating deep investigation into new therapeutic treatments.
Way 3: Biological Products - They are genetically modified to act as bioreactors, producing highly valuable human medical proteins, such as alpha-1-antitrypsin used to treat severe emphysema.
Way 4: Vaccine Safety Testing - Transgenic mice are heavily utilized to test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines (like the polio vaccine) before they are ever administered to humans.

questions.solution: Transgenic animals offer immense biotechnological benefits to humanity in several profound ways. Firstly, they act as critical models for the Study of Disease; they are genetically engineered to perfectly mimic human diseases like cancer or cystic fibrosis, allowing researchers to deeply investigate disease progression and test novel treatments. Secondly, they are utilized for the production of Biological Products; certain transgenic animals are modified to act as living bioreactors, safely secreting highly valuable human medical proteins into their milk, such as the human protein alpha-1-antitrypsin, which is crucially used to treat severe emphysema. Thirdly, they play a vital role in Vaccine Safety Testing; incredibly sensitive transgenic mice are heavily utilized in pharmaceutical labs to thoroughly test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines, completely ensuring they are safe before ever attempting clinical trials on humans.
questions.solution_hindi:
पारजीवी जंतु (Transgenic animals) मनुष्यों के लिए कई प्रकार से उपयोगी सिद्ध हो सकते हैं: 
1) रोगों का अध्ययन (Study of Disease): पारजीवी जंतुओं को विशेष रूप से मानव रोगों (जैसे कैंसर, सिस्टिक फाइब्रोसिस) के मॉडल के रूप में कार्य करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया जाता है, जिससे बीमारी के विकास का अध्ययन करने और नए उपचार खोजने में मदद मिलती है।
2) जैविक उत्पाद (Biological Products): कुछ पारजीवी जंतुओं का उपयोग मूल्यवान मानव चिकित्सा प्रोटीन का उत्पादन करने के लिए किया जाता है, जैसे एम्फाइसेमा (emphysema) के इलाज के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाने वाला अल्फा-1-एंटीट्रिप्सिन (alpha-1-antitrypsin)।
3) टीकों की सुरक्षा का परीक्षण (Vaccine Safety Testing): मनुष्यों पर इस्तेमाल होने से पहले टीकों (जैसे पोलियो का टीका) की सुरक्षा और प्रभावशीलता का कड़ाई से परीक्षण करने के लिए पारजीवी चूहों का उपयोग किया जाता है।

questions.text: प्रत्येक के एक-एक उदाहरण की सहायता से आनुवंशिक, जातीय तथा पारिस्थितिक स्तर पर जैव-विविधता के स्तरों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the level of biodiversity at genetic, species and ecological levels with the help of one example each.

key_points: Explain Genetic diversity: It is the immense variation of genes existing within a single species. Example: The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria exhibits high genetic variation in the potency of its active chemical reserpine across the Himalayas, OR India has 50,000 distinct genetically different strains of rice.

Explain Species diversity: It is the stark variety of different species existing within a specific region. Example: The Western Ghats exhibit a significantly greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats.

Explain Ecological diversity: It refers to the massive variation in distinct ecosystems within a geographical area. Example: India boasts a massive ecological diversity featuring deserts, rainforests, mangroves, and coral reefs, compared to a physically homogeneous country like Norway.

questions.solution: Biodiversity fundamentally exists at three distinct, interconnected levels. Firstly, Genetic diversity refers to the immense variation of genes and alleles existing strictly within a single species. For example, the medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria exhibits profound genetic variation in the concentration and potency of its active chemical, reserpine, across different Himalayan ranges. Alternatively, India famously cultivates over 50,000 genetically different strains of rice. Secondly, Species diversity denotes the absolute variety and richness of distinctly different species existing within a specific geographic region. For instance, the lush Western Ghats of India exhibit a remarkably higher amphibian species diversity compared to the drier Eastern Ghats. Lastly, Ecological diversity refers to the macroscopic variation in entirely different ecosystems or biomes within a broad geographical area. For example, India boasts a massively rich ecological diversity featuring harsh deserts, dense rainforests, complex mangroves, and vibrant coral reefs, which is vastly superior to the physically homogeneous ecology found in a Scandinavian country like Norway.
questions.solution_hindi: जैव-विविधता मुख्य रूप से तीन अलग-अलग स्तरों पर मौजूद होती है। 1) आनुवंशिक विविधता (Genetic diversity): यह एक ही प्रजाति के भीतर जीनों की विविधता को दर्शाता है। उदाहरण के लिए, हिमालय में पाया जाने वाला औषधीय पौधा राउवोल्फिया वोमिटोरिया (Rauwolfia vomitoria) अपने सक्रिय रसायन रेसरपाइन की शक्ति और सांद्रता में भारी आनुवंशिक विविधता दर्शाता है। 2) जातीय विविधता (Species diversity): यह एक विशिष्ट क्षेत्र के भीतर विभिन्न प्रजातियों की विविधता है। उदाहरण के लिए, पश्चिमी घाट में पूर्वी घाट की तुलना में उभयचर (amphibian) प्रजातियों की विविधता बहुत अधिक है। 3) पारिस्थितिक विविधता (Ecological diversity): यह एक विस्तृत भौगोलिक क्षेत्र के भीतर विभिन्न पारिस्थितिक तंत्रों में भिन्नता है। उदाहरण के लिए, भारत में पारिस्थितिक विविधता बहुत अधिक है क्योंकि यहाँ रेगिस्तान, वर्षा वन, मैंग्रोव और प्रवाल भित्तियाँ पाई जाती हैं, जबकि नॉर्वे जैसे देश में ऐसी विविधता नहीं है।

The process of copying genetic information from template strand of DNA into RNA is called transcription. It is mediated by RNA polymerase. Transcription takes place in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. In transcription, only a segment of DNA and only one of the strands is copied into RNA.

sub_questions.text: (क) क्या कारण है कि, डीएनए रज्जुक की 3'->5' ध्रुवत्व वाली रज्जुक ही अनुलेखित होती है और 5'->3' ध्रुवत्व वाली दूसरी रज्जुक से अनुलेखन नहीं होता ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Why is the strand of DNA with 3'->5' polarity transcribed and not the other strand of 5'->3' polarity?

key_points: Explain that the enzyme DNA-dependent RNA polymerase strictly catalyzes polymerization only in one single direction, which is precisely the 5'->3' direction.
Conclude that therefore, only the DNA strand with the opposing 3'->5' polarity can act as the physical template for this synthesis.

sub_questions.solution: The DNA strand with 3' to 5' polarity is exclusively transcribed because the primary synthesizing enzyme, DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, contains a strict biological limitation: it can only catalyze nucleotide polymerization in one specific direction, which is firmly 5' to 3'. Therefore, it absolutely requires the antiparallel strand possessing the 3' to 5' polarity to serve as its reading template.

sub_questions.text: (ख) (i) समबंधन (स्प्लाइसिंग) के लिए एचएनआरएनए (hnRNA) की आवश्यकता क्यों होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) (i) Why is hnRNA required to undergo splicing?

key_points: Explain that hnRNA (the primary transcript) contains both essential coding sequences called exons and useless non-coding sequences called introns.
State that splicing is absolutely required to physically cut out the non-coding introns and meticulously join the exons in a defined sequence, rendering the mRNA fully functional.

sub_questions.solution: In eukaryotic cells, the initial RNA transcript, known as hnRNA, is heavily flawed because it contains functional, protein-coding sequences known as exons violently interspersed with completely useless, non-coding sequences known as introns. Thus, hnRNA is required to undergo the complex splicing process to systematically cut out and entirely remove all the non-coding introns, while meticulously joining the remaining exons together in a precise, unbroken sequence to form functional mRNA.

sub_questions.solution: In addition to splicing, the fragile hnRNA must undergo two vital, protective post-transcriptional modifications to become a fully stable and functional mRNA capable of leaving the nucleus. The first process is Capping, where an unusual nucleotide (specifically methyl guanosine triphosphate) is permanently added to the 5' end of the transcript. The second process is Tailing, wherein a long, protective string of adenylate residues (a poly-A tail) is systematically added to the 3' end in a strictly template-independent manner.

sub_questions.text_english: (c) Why is only one strand of the DNA transcribed? Give two reasons.

key_points: Reason 1: If both strands acted as templates simultaneously, they would wildly code for two entirely different RNA molecules with completely different sequences, creating chaotic proteins that disrupt the genetic information transfer machinery.

Reason 2: The two resulting RNA molecules produced simultaneously would be completely complementary to each other and would instantly base-pair to form a useless double-stranded RNA molecule, heavily blocking the crucial translation process.

sub_questions.solution: Only one strand of DNA is transcribed primarily for two critical biological reasons to avoid total cellular chaos. Firstly, if both DNA strands simultaneously acted as templates, they would wildly transcribe two totally different RNA molecules with completely distinct sequences. This would result in a single DNA segment paradoxically coding for two entirely different proteins, catastrophically complicating the strict genetic information transfer machinery. Secondly, because these two newly synthesized RNA strands would possess perfectly complementary sequences, they would immediately bind together to form a highly stable, useless double-stranded RNA molecule. This structural formation would fundamentally block the ribosomes, totally preventing the mRNA from being successfully translated into any protein.

key_points: Cross 1 (Pea): Pure Violet (VV) x Pure White (vv). F1 is all Violet (Vv). Selfing F1 gives F2 phenotypic ratio of 3 Violet : 1 White, and genotypic ratio of 1 VV : 2 Vv : 1 vv.
Cross 2 (Antirrhinum): Pure Red (RR) x Pure White (rr). F1 is all Pink (Rr). Selfing F1 gives F2 phenotypic ratio of 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White, and genotypic ratio of 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr.
Comment on Pea inheritance: This demonstrates Complete Dominance, where the dominant allele (V) completely masks the expression of the recessive allele (v) in the heterozygous state.

Comment on Antirrhinum inheritance: This demonstrates Incomplete Dominance, where the dominant allele (R) is unable to completely mask the recessive allele (r), resulting in a visibly blended intermediate phenotype (Pink) in the heterozygote.

sub_questions.solution:
In the case of the classic pea plant, working out the monohybrid cross involves mating a homozygous dominant plant with violet flowers (VV) and a homozygous recessive plant with white flowers (vv). The entire F1 generation overwhelmingly displays the violet phenotype due to their heterozygous genotype (Vv). When these F1 hybrids are self-pollinated, the resulting F2 generation sharply exhibits a phenotypic ratio of 3 Violet to 1 White, with a genotypic ratio of 1 VV : 2 Vv : 1 vv. This specific inheritance pattern robustly demonstrates Complete Dominance, where the dominant allele completely overwhelms the recessive allele.
Conversely, when conducting a monohybrid cross in snapdragon (Antirrhinum) plants regarding flower color, a homozygous plant with red flowers (RR) is crossed with a homozygous plant with white flowers (rr). The F1 offspring unexpectedly do not resemble either parent; instead, they all display an intermediate pink phenotype with a heterozygous genotype (Rr). Upon self-pollinating these F1 pink plants, the F2 generation yields a surprising phenotypic ratio of 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White, perfectly matching its genotypic ratio of 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. This specific pattern distinctly demonstrates Incomplete Dominance, a phenomenon where the dominant allele fails to completely mask the recessive allele, culminating in a blended, intermediate physical trait.

(ii) Name the phenomenon that leads to situations like 'XO' abnormality in humans. Also name this genetic disorder. How are individuals with an XO chromosomal abnormality affected? Write its symptoms as well as karyotype.

key_points: Difference: Mendelian disorders are fundamentally caused by an alteration or mutation strictly in a single, specific gene on a chromosome. Chromosomal disorders are catastrophically caused by the massive absence, excess, or physically abnormal arrangement of one or entire multiple chromosomes.
Examples: Haemophilia or Sickle-cell anaemia (Mendelian); Down's syndrome or Turner's syndrome (Chromosomal).
Phenomenon for XO: Aneuploidy, specifically resulting from the disastrous non-disjunction (failure of segregation) of sex chromosomes during meiotic gametogenesis.
Disorder name: Turner's syndrome.

Symptoms: Such affected individuals are always sterile females exhibiting profoundly rudimentary ovaries, a noticeable lack of secondary sexual characters, heavily stunted short stature, and a characteristically webbed neck.
Karyotype: 45, XO (possessing only 45 chromosomes instead of 46).

sub_questions.solution:
Mendelian disorders and chromosomal disorders differ vastly in their structural origins. A Mendelian disorder is fundamentally determined by a precise alteration or mutation strictly restricted to a single gene located on a chromosome, allowing it to be traced through family trees using standard pedigree analysis. A classic example is Haemophilia. In stark contrast, a chromosomal disorder is a macroscopic defect brutally caused by the complete absence, an anomalous excess, or a severely abnormal physical arrangement of one or several entire chromosomes, throwing hundreds of genes out of balance simultaneously. A prominent example is Down's syndrome. 
Addressing the 'XO' abnormality: this severe condition is generated by a biological phenomenon termed aneuploidy, which specifically occurs due to non-disjunction—the disastrous failure of the sex chromosomes to segregate properly during meiosis while forming gametes. This specific genetic disorder is formally diagnosed as Turner's syndrome. An individual suffering from this chromosomal abnormality is phenotypically female but faces massive developmental setbacks. She is completely sterile due to the presence of profoundly rudimentary ovaries. Her physical symptoms heavily include a noticeable lack of normal secondary sexual characteristics, a markedly short physical stature, and a characteristically broad, webbed neck. Because she entirely lacks the second X chromosome, her total chromosome count is diminished, making her karyotype accurately described as 45, XO.

The debilitating disease filariasis is biologically caused by two specific species of parasitic filarial worms, scientifically named Wuchereria bancrofti and Wuchereria malayi. When these invasive worms establish themselves within a human host, they typically lodge deeply within the delicate lymphatic vessels, particularly of the lower limbs. Over many years, they aggressively provoke a slowly developing but severe chronic inflammation, which brutally blocks lymph drainage. This catastrophic blockage leads to massive swelling and gross anatomical deformities of the legs and genital organs, a severe condition universally recognized as elephantiasis. In the broader context of human immune defense: Histamine is a powerful chemical heavily sourced and secreted by specialized mast cells and basophils. Its primary role is to act as a potent vasodilator during violent allergic reactions, triggering rapid, localized inflammatory responses that aggressively recruit other immune cells to the affected site. Interferons are specialized antiviral proteins heavily sourced and secreted exclusively by host cells that have already been tragically infected by a virus. sub_questions.text_english: (a) Briefly explain the events of fertilisation and implantation in an adult human female.

key_points: Describe Fertilisation: Fusion of a sperm with an ovum specifically in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube.
Detail acrosomal reaction: The sperm physically penetrates the tough zona pellucida, instantly causing a cortical reaction that entirely prevents polyspermy.

Detail meiotic completion: Sperm entry decisively triggers the completion of meiosis II in the secondary oocyte, leading to the formation of a haploid ovum and second polar body, finally resulting in a diploid zygote.
Describe Cleavage: The zygote undergoes rapid mitotic divisions traveling down the oviduct, transforming into a morula and then a blastocyst.

Describe Implantation: The outer trophoblast layer of the blastocyst firmly attaches to the vascular endometrium of the uterus. The uterine cells then aggressively divide and cover the blastocyst, embedding it entirely to establish pregnancy.

sub_questions.solution: In an adult human female, the highly complex biological event of fertilisation strictly occurs within the ampullary region of the fallopian tube when a motile sperm successfully contacts the secondary oocyte. The sperm's acrosome aggressively releases enzymes to physically penetrate the thick, protective zona pellucida layer. This immediate penetration violently alters the membrane structure, permanently preventing the entry of any additional sperms (polyspermy). Furthermore, the sperm's entry rapidly triggers the long-arrested secondary oocyte to finally complete its second meiotic division, creating a mature haploid ovum which instantly fuses with the sperm nucleus to forge a diploid zygote. Immediately following this, the zygote embarks on a journey down the oviduct towards the uterus, undergoing rapid, successive mitotic divisions known as cleavage to form a solid mass called a morula, which further hollows out into a blastocyst. Implantation culminates when this blastocyst reaches the uterus. The blastocyst's sticky outer cellular layer, the trophoblast, firmly anchors itself directly onto the nutrient-rich uterine endometrium. The stimulated uterine cells aggressively divide, physically surrounding and deeply embedding the entire blastocyst into the uterine wall, permanently establishing a stable pregnancy.

hCG; LH; FSH; Relaxin.

key_points: Arrange the strict sequence: FSH -> LH -> hCG -> Relaxin.
FSH Source & Function: Secreted by Anterior Pituitary; it actively stimulates the massive growth and maturation of ovarian follicles.
LH Source & Function: Secreted by Anterior Pituitary; a massive mid-cycle surge triggers the rupture of the mature follicle (ovulation) and maintains the corpus luteum.
hCG Source & Function: Secreted by Placenta (or trophoblast); it mimics LH to sustain the corpus luteum heavily during early pregnancy to continue massive progesterone secretion.

Relaxin Source & Function: Secreted primarily by Ovary/Placenta in the later phases of pregnancy; it fundamentally softens and relaxes the pelvic ligaments to heavily assist in parturition (childbirth).

sub_questions.solution:
Taking into account the entire reproductive cycle leading up to and finalizing a pregnancy, the correct chronological sequence of secretion for these critical hormones is: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), followed by Luteinizing Hormone (LH), then human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG), and finally Relaxin. 
Detailing their biological sources and vital functions: 
1. FSH is secreted deeply by the anterior pituitary gland; its primary function is to aggressively stimulate the growth, structural development, and maturation of ovarian follicles. 
2. LH is also secreted by the anterior pituitary; a sudden, massive surge in LH mid-cycle decisively triggers ovulation (the rupture of the Graafian follicle) and subsequently transforms the remnants into the corpus luteum. 
3. hCG is secreted exclusively by the newly formed placenta (trophoblast cells) following implantation; it acts to aggressively maintain the corpus luteum during early pregnancy, ensuring it continues to secrete massive amounts of progesterone to prevent endometrial shedding. 
4. Relaxin is secreted predominantly by the ovary and placenta during the much later stages of pregnancy; its paramount physiological role is to significantly soften and relax the tough pelvic ligaments, thereby safely facilitating the demanding process of parturition (childbirth).
